response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_reb, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net FROM fees GROUP BY orderslink), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_net) AS bm FROM per_order) SELECT AVG(p.avg_reb) AS avg_of_avg_rebtotal, AVG(p.avg_net) AS avg_of_avg_net_rate, AVG(p.avg_net - b.bm) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN bench b WHERE p.avg_net > b.bm

assumptions.assumption: A fee record's net rate (feerate - rebrate) is NULL if either value is NULL, so such records are skipped in that order's average net rate. An order whose records all have a NULL net rate has a NULL average and is left out of the benchmark and the comparison.
Fee records with a NULL orderslink form a single group, which counts as one order in the benchmark.
